title: Trump Threatened Drug Makers With 100% Tariffs While Pretending It Was About Lower Prices
description_short: Trump Threatened Drug Makers With 100% Tariffs While Pretending It Was About Lower Prices
description_medium: On April 2, 2026, Trump threatened a 100% tariff on branded drugs and active ingredients from companies without White House pricing deals. Generics, which make up more than 90% of U.S. medicines, would be exempt for at least a year. Companies agreeing to pricing terms and domestic production could also avoid the tariff.
description_long: On April 2, 2026, Trump announced a threatened 100% tariff on pharmaceutical companies that had not reached agreements to lower U.S. drug prices. The Guardian reported that the proposed levy applied to branded medicines and their active ingredients, while generics—which account for more than 90% of medicines sold in the United States—would be exempt for at least a year. Orphan, veterinary, and some specialty drugs also qualified for exemptions. Companies entering White House pricing agreements and producing drugs domestically could avoid the tariff; manufacturers planning to expand U.S. production would face a lower rate that could rise to 100% after four years. Larger firms had 120 days to negotiate, and smaller companies 180 days. The policy announcement therefore combined price negotiations with import penalties and incentives for domestic manufacturing. It was a threat with stated exemptions and negotiation periods, not evidence that all affected companies paid the tariff or that patients’ prices changed. The announcement presented the tariff threat as a way to secure lower U.S. drug prices; the report describes the policy terms and its stated rationale.

preserved_fields.title: Trump Threatened Drug Makers With 100% Tariffs While Pretending It Was About Lower Prices
preserved_fields.description_short: Trump Threatened Drug Makers With 100% Tariffs While Pretending It Was About Lower Prices

notes: Needs context: the Guardian report describes price agreements as the stated purpose but does not support the title’s claim that Trump was pretending. Proposed correction: remove the assertion about deceptive intent unless direct evidence supports it.

title: The Birth of Roy Cohn: Architect of Trumpism
description_short: The Birth of Roy Cohn: Architect of Trumpism
description_medium: On February 20, 1927, Roy Cohn was born in New York to Judge Albert C. Cohn and Dora Cohn. He would grow up to become one of the most notoriously corrupt and ruthless attorneys in New York City history. Decades later, Cohn would become the defining mentor to a young Donald Trump, teaching him the dark arts of total legal warfare: always attack, never apologize, and claim victory regardless of the facts. Cohn’s influence laid the structural foundation for the authoritarian tactics Trump would later deploy in the White House.

title: Trump meets love interest at Mogilevich's Moscow hotel
description_short: Trump meets love interest at Mogilevich's Moscow hotel
description_medium: A TrumpFile timeline says Donald Trump attended a party in the “Library” room of Moscow’s Baltschug-Kempinski hotel during a November 1996 visit. Its account does not establish that Semion Mogilevich owned the hotel or that Trump met a romantic interest there. The Senate inquiry into Trump and Russia does not verify those details of this anecdote.
description_long: A TrumpFile timeline dated November 6, 1996, recounts that Donald Trump attended a party in the “Library” room at Moscow’s Baltschug-Kempinski hotel during a visit to the city. The timeline also claims that the hotel was owned by Semion Mogilevich and that Trump met a romantic interest there, but it provides no evidence of the hotel’s ownership, a guest list, or the alleged relationship. Those claims are central to the title and cannot be treated as established facts from this account alone. A later Senate Intelligence Committee report examined contacts and business interests involving Trump and Russia; that broader inquiry does not verify the details of this particular party. The event can be stated only as the timeline’s account of Trump attending a hotel gathering. Confirmation of the ownership claim or a personal encounter would require records or independent reporting specific to the trip. Without those records, the ownership and meeting claims remain unverified.

preserved_fields.title: Trump meets love interest at Mogilevich's Moscow hotel
preserved_fields.description_short: Trump meets love interest at Mogilevich's Moscow hotel

notes: Needs context: the timeline recounts a party but does not substantiate Mogilevich’s hotel ownership or a romantic meeting. The Senate report does not establish those anecdotal claims. Proposed correction: retitle around the reported hotel visit unless trip-specific evidence supports the stronger claims.

title: Trump: Rudy Giuliani takes Trump's jet for NYC trip to Israel
description_short: Trump: Rudy Giuliani takes Trump's jet for NYC trip to Israel
description_medium: New York City Mayor Rudy Giuliani traveled to Israel on December 8, 2001, aboard Donald Trump’s private jet, about three months after the September 11 attacks. His party included girlfriend Judith “Judi” Nathan, local law-enforcement officers, and others. Reports differed on whether Trump offered the plane or Giuliani asked to borrow it; the accounts do not state who paid for the trip.
description_long: On December 8, 2001, New York City Mayor Rudy Giuliani traveled to Israel aboard Donald Trump’s private jet, roughly three months after the September 11 attacks. Giuliani was accompanied by his girlfriend, Judith “Judi” Nathan, local law-enforcement officers, and several others. The trip was reported as an official city visit. Accounts differed about how Giuliani obtained the aircraft: some said Trump offered it, while others said Giuliani asked to borrow it. The reports do not resolve that discrepancy or identify who paid for the flight, give a full itinerary, or explain the specific official purpose. Those details would matter when evaluating the use of a private aircraft for a public official’s trip, but the available account does not establish an ethics violation or improper benefit. The documented event is Giuliani’s journey to Israel aboard Trump’s jet; the arrangements and any financial consequences remain unclear.

preserved_fields.title: Trump: Rudy Giuliani takes Trump's jet for NYC trip to Israel
preserved_fields.description_short: Trump: Rudy Giuliani takes Trump's jet for NYC trip to Israel

notes: The reports establish the trip and use of Trump’s aircraft, but differ on how Giuliani obtained the plane and do not establish who paid.

title: Trump: Leaked documents confirm Mogilevich controls Russian-Ukrainian energy giant
description_short: Trump: Leaked documents confirm Mogilevich controls Russian-Ukrainian energy giant
description_medium: A timeline says documents leaked in late 2010 included then–prime minister Yulia Tymoshenko’s claim that criminal networks were behind RosUkrEnergo. It attributes to Dmitry Firtash a statement that Semion Mogilevich was connected to the energy company. These are reported claims, not proof of Mogilevich’s control, and the account does not connect the episode to Trump.
description_long: A timeline dated December 2010 describes leaked material concerning RosUkrEnergo, a Russian-Ukrainian energy company. It says then–prime minister Yulia Tymoshenko claimed to have documentation that powerful criminal structures were behind the company, and reports that Ukrainian businessman Dmitry Firtash—described as holding a 50% stake—told her that Semion Mogilevich was connected to it. These are two separate claims relayed by the timeline: Tymoshenko’s statement about criminal structures and Firtash’s reported statement about Mogilevich. Neither is itself a corporate ownership record, and the underlying documents are not reproduced in the linked account. Tymoshenko’s statement and the attributed conversation do not by themselves establish that Mogilevich controlled RosUkrEnergo. The account does not link the alleged leak to Donald Trump. Without the documents and information about their provenance, the reported connection does not establish who controlled the company.

preserved_fields.title: Trump: Leaked documents confirm Mogilevich controls Russian-Ukrainian energy giant
preserved_fields.description_short: Trump: Leaked documents confirm Mogilevich controls Russian-Ukrainian energy giant

notes: Needs context: the linked timeline does not reproduce the alleged documents, and its synopsis does not connect the event to Trump. Proposed correction: remove the Trump prefix and avoid “confirm” unless the documents and provenance are provided.
